7: Autonomous bug fixer loop plugin for Google Antigravity (AGY). It provides a 3-loop background agent system that autonomously triages, fixes, tests, and opens pull requests for small bugs and TODOs in a target repository while human engineers focus on major feature work and architectural PRs.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## Overview
12: 
13: Modern software development often suffers from an accumulation of small bugs, DX papercuts, and un-ignored test cases that distract maintainers from core product development. `bug-fixer-loop` operates as a trusted, guard-railed junior engineer:
14: 
15: - **Runs in background sidecars** on bounded cron schedules.
16: - **Respects human maintainer PR priority** via an active-PR exclusion zone.
17: - **Guarantees security & boundary defense** through PreToolUse hooks, safe ingestion filters, and mandatory test passes.
18: - **Never auto-merges**: All changes are delivered as clean, atomic Pull Requests for human review.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## Getting Started
23: 
24: ### 1. Install
25: ```bash
26: ./scripts/install.sh
27: ```
28: The plugin ships **disabled** by default. No sidecars will run until you configure and enable it.
29: 
30: ### 2. Configure
31: ```bash
32: ./scripts/configure.sh --repo <owner/repo> --repo-dir <path>
33: ```
34: The wizard validates connectivity, creates labels, and optionally sets up an isolated worktree.
35: 
36: ### 3. Enable
37: ```bash
38: agy plugin enable bug-fixer-loop
39: ```
40: The 3 background sidecars will now run on their configured schedules.
41: 
42: ### 4. Pause / Resume
43: ```bash
44: agy plugin disable bug-fixer-loop   # pause
45: agy plugin enable bug-fixer-loop    # resume
46: ```
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## Architecture
51: 
52: The plugin implements a deterministic 3-loop engineering cycle:
53: 
54: ```mermaid
55: flowchart TD
56:     subgraph GitHub ["GitHub Repository"]
57:         Issues["Open Issues & PR Feedback"]
58:         PRs["Pull Requests"]
59:         HumanReview["Maintainer Review & Merge"]
60:     end
61: 
62:     subgraph Security ["Security & Ingestion Boundary"]
63:         SafeIngest["safe_ingest.py\n(Maintainer Approval Gate & Secret Redaction)"]
64:         PreToolGate["pre_tool_gate.py\n(PreToolUse Invariant Enforcement)"]
65:     end
66: 
67:     subgraph Loops ["Bug Fixer 4-Loop Engine"]
68:         TriageSidecar["Triage Loop\n(Hourly cron: 0 * * * *)\nClassifies auto-fixable vs human-required"]
69:         EngineeringSidecar["Engineering Loop\n(Every 10 min: */10 * * * *)\nClaims issue, branches, fixes, tests, PRs"]
70:         PRReviewSidecar["PR Review Loop\n(Every 15 min)\nAdversarial architect review of draft PRs"]
71:         TrajectoryReviewSidecar["Trajectory Review Loop\n(Daily: 0 18 * * *)\nAudits test quality & trajectory health"]
72:     end
73: 
74:     Issues --> SafeIngest
75:     SafeIngest --> TriageSidecar
76:     TriageSidecar -- "Labels auto-fixable" --> Issues
77:     TriageSidecar -- "Labels human-required (e.g. overlap)" --> Issues
78:     SafeIngest --> EngineeringSidecar
79:     EngineeringSidecar --> PreToolGate
80:     PreToolGate -- "Verified Clean & Tested" --> PRs
81:     PRs --> PRReviewSidecar
82:     PRReviewSidecar -- "Approves or requests iteration" --> EngineeringSidecar
83:     PRs --> HumanReview
84:     HumanReview -- "Merges PR" --> GitHub
85:     TrajectoryReviewSidecar -. "Audits fix quality" .-> EngineeringSidecar
86: ```
87: 
88: ---
89: 
90: ## The 4 Loops
91: 
92: ### 1. Triage Loop (`bug-fixer-triage-loop`)
93: - **Schedule:** Hourly (`0 * * * *`)
94: - **Execution Role:** Evaluates newly created or unclassified issues.
95: - **Responsibilities:**
96:   - Safely reads open issues via `safe_ingest.py`.
97:   - Checks for exclusion labels (`hardware-required`, `P1-blocker`, etc.).
98:   - Cross-references the maintainer's open PR file lists to exclude any issue touching overlapping modules.
99:   - Labels candidates as `auto-fixable` (bounded, single-module bugs with clear criteria) or `human-required` (architectural, multi-module, or ambiguous issues).
100: 
101: ### 2. Engineering Loop (`bug-fixer-engineering-loop`)
102: - **Schedule:** Every 2 hours (`30 */2 * * *`)
103: - **Execution Role:** Implements surgical fixes and delivers pull requests.
104: - **Responsibilities:**
105:   - Enforces PR concurrency caps (`max_concurrent_prs`).
106:   - Prioritizes remediating feedback on existing agent PRs before picking new work.
107:   - Claims highest-priority `auto-fixable` issue from `origin/main` in a dedicated worktree.
108:   - Implements the fix and executes the mandatory `test_command` (e.g. `pio test -e native`).
109:   - Audits staged files for leaks with `pre_tool_gate.py --scan-only`.
110:   - Opens an atomic PR titled `[BugFixer] Resolves #<number>` containing test output.
111: 
112: ### 3. PR Review Loop (`bug-fixer-pr-review-loop`)
113: - **Schedule:** Every 15 minutes
114: - **Execution Role:** Adversarial architect review of bug-fixer draft PRs.
115: - **Responsibilities:**
116:   - Polls for un-reviewed draft PRs with the `bug-fixer` label.
117:   - Spawns an Architect review conversation for each eligible draft.
118:   - Tracks review rounds and escalates to `needs-human-intervention` after max rounds.
119: 
120: ### 4. Trajectory Review Loop (`bug-fixer-trajectory-loop`)
121: - **Schedule:** Daily (`0 18 * * *`)
122: - **Execution Role:** Audits quality trends and agent trajectory logs.
123: - **Responsibilities:**
124:   - Audits test suite quality to ensure assertions test real behavior rather than tautologies.
125:   - Validates that leak audit receipts were consistently stamped.
126:   - Flags repeated test escalation patterns to prevent wasted agent cycles.
127: 
128: ---
129: 
130: ## Security Model
131: 
132: The security architecture provides three layers of defense against prompt injection, model drift, and unauthorized mutations:
133: 
134: 1. **PreToolUse Hook Gate (`pre_tool_gate.py`)**:
135:    - **Specification Immutability:** Denies all writes and shell mutations (`sed -i`, `>`, `rm`, `cp`) targeting the project specification (`docs/design_specification.md`).
136:    - **Protected Files:** Prohibits modification of sensitive human artifacts listed in `protected_files`.
137:    - **Host Script Self-Defense:** Blocks autonomous edits to `pre_tool_gate.py` and `safe_ingest.py`.
138:    - **Forbidden Command Interception:** Blocks `gh pr merge`, `gh stack merge`, `gh pr review --approve`, `gh issue reopen`, and raw `gh issue/pr list|view`.
139:    - **Fake Approval Injection Defense:** Blocks posting approval commands (`approved`, `/approve`).
140: 
141: 2. **Deterministic Safe Ingestion (`safe_ingest.py`)**:
142:    - **Maintainer Approval Gate:** External issues and PRs require explicit maintainer approval before un-redacted titles, bodies, and comments are admitted into model context.
143:    - **TOCTOU Protection:** Compares timestamps (`createdAt`, `lastEditedAt`, `pushedDate`) against the approval timestamp to detect post-approval edits and force-pushes.
144:    - **Secret Redaction:** Free-text fields are sanitized against configurable `leak_patterns`.
145: 
146: 3. **Git Hooks & Cryptographic Receipts**:
147:    - Staged tree SHA receipts (`.git/leak_audit_receipt.json`) are stamped by the `leak-auditor` agent and verified before push.
148:    - **No Auto-Merge Policy:** Autonomous agents are technically blocked from merging. Merging remains strictly a human action.
149:

34: ## Core Concepts
35: 
36: An Antigravity **plugin** is a namespaced, shareable bundle that packages **skills**, **rules**, **hooks**, and optionally **MCP server configs** and **sidecar definitions** into a single deployable unit. Plugins are the recommended way to distribute complex agent behaviours.
37: 
38: A plugin has two distinct concerns:
39: 
40: | Concern | Where it lives | Mutable? | Committed? |
41: |---------|---------------|:--------:|:----------:|
42: | **Plugin code** (scripts, skills, rules, hooks templates) | `.agents/plugins/<name>/` | ❌ Immutable | ✅ Submodule |
43: | **Instance state** (config, claims, cooldown files) | `.agents/plugins/<name>-workspace/` | ✅ Mutable | Config: ✅ / State: ❌ |
44: 
45: The plugin directory is a **git submodule** (or standalone clone). It is treated as read-only after installation. All mutable state — configuration, runtime locks, circuit breaker files — lives in a separate **workspace directory** alongside it.

100: ### Key Principle: Path Derivation
101: 
102: Every path is derivable from the config file's own location:
103: 
104: ```
105: config.json is at:  <repo>/.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/config.json
106:                      │
107:                      ├── parent     = STATE_DIR  (.../bug-fixer-loop-workspace/)
108:                      ├── parent²    = plugins/
109:                      ├── parent³    = .agents/

112:                      STATE_DIR sibling = PLUGIN_DIR (.../bug-fixer-loop-plugin/)
113: ```

116: 
117: ```python

119: STATE_DIR = CONFIG_FILE.parent
120: REPO_DIR = STATE_DIR.parent.parent.parent
121: PLUGIN_DIR = STATE_DIR.parent / "bug-fixer-loop-plugin"
122: ```

126: ## Discovery & Loading
127: 
128: Antigravity discovers plugins by traversing the `.agents/plugins/` directory tree. Each plugin directory must contain a `plugin.json` manifest:
129: 
130: ```json
131: {
132:   "name": "bug-fixer-loop"
133: }
134: ```
135: 
136: When discovered and enabled, Antigravity automatically ingests:
137: - **Skills** from `plugins/<name>/skills/` (progressive disclosure — name + description loaded, full content on activation)
138: - **Rules** from `plugins/<name>/rules/` (merged into active rule set)
139: - **Hooks** from `plugins/<name>/hooks.json` (registered for lifecycle events)
140: - **MCP servers** from `plugins/<name>/mcp_config.json` (launched and tools exposed)
141: 
142: ### Loading Priority (highest → lowest)
143: 
144: 1. **Workspace project** — `.agents/` walking up from CWD to repo root
145: 2. **Declared configs** — explicit `skills.json` or `plugins.json`
146: 3. **Global discovery** — `~/.gemini/config/`
147: 4. **Built-in customisations** — bundled with Antigravity
148: 5. **Global declared configs** — global JSON configs
149: 
150: Workspace-scoped customisations always win over global ones.
151: 
152: ### Enabling / Disabling
153: 
154: Plugin state is recorded in `~/.gemini/config/config.json`:
155: 
156: ```json
157: {
158:   "plugins": {
159:     "bug-fixer-loop-plugin": { "enabled": true }
160:   }
161: }
162: ```
163: 
164: Toggle via CLI: `agy plugin enable bug-fixer-loop` / `agy plugin disable bug-fixer-loop`.

168: ## The Immutable Plugin Root Principle
169: 
170: > **The plugin directory is read-only after installation.**
171: 
172: This is the single most important architectural rule. The plugin directory (`bug-fixer-loop-plugin/`) is typically a git submodule. Nothing should write to it:
173: 
174: - ❌ No `config.json` with instance values
175: - ❌ No runtime state files (claims, locks, cooldowns)
176: - ❌ No `install.sh` writing back into it
177: - ❌ No sed/templating modifying files in-place
178: 
179: Scripts, skills, and agents are **used in-place** — never copied to global directories. The plugin root is the single source of truth for code.

243: ## Hooks
244: 
245: Hooks are lifecycle interceptors that run external commands at specific points in the agent's execution. The plugin defines hooks in `hooks.json` with **placeholder paths**:
246: 
247: ```json
248: {
249:   "bug-fixer-file-gate": {
250:     "PreToolUse": [{
251:       "matcher": "write_to_file|replace_file_content",
252:       "hooks": [{
253:         "type": "command",
254:         "command": "python3 <plugin_dir>/scripts/pre_tool_gate.py",
255:         "timeout": 10
256:       }]
257:     }]
258:   }
259: }
260: ```
261: 
262: ### Path Resolution
263: 
264: The `<plugin_dir>` placeholder is resolved by `install.sh` at install time, producing a workspace-scoped `hooks.json` at `.agents/hooks.json`.
265: 
266: **Critical rule:** Hooks must be installed to the **workspace** `.agents/hooks.json`, never to the global `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`. A broken global hook bricks every project on the machine.
267: 
268: ### Hook Working Directory
269: 
270: The hook command's working directory is set to the directory containing `hooks.json`. If hooks are installed at `.agents/hooks.json`, the cwd is `.agents/`.
271: 
272: ### PreToolUse Contract
273: 
274: The `pre_tool_gate.py` hook receives tool call details on stdin and returns a decision on stdout:
275: 
276: ```json
277: // stdin (from Antigravity)
278: {
279:   "toolCall": {"name": "write_to_file", "args": {"TargetFile": "/path/to/file.py"}},
280:   "conversationId": "...",
281:   "workspacePaths": ["/path/to/repo"]
282: }
283: 
284: // stdout (from hook script)
285: {"decision": "allow"}     // or "deny" with "reason"
286: ```

329: ## Sidecars & Dispatchers
330: 
331: Sidecars are **background processes managed by Antigravity's runtime**. They are the mechanism for running recurring automated tasks — scheduled builds, periodic issue triage, cron-driven health checks — without requiring a user to be actively chatting.
332: 
333: ### How Antigravity Discovers Sidecars
334: 
335: Antigravity scans specific directories on startup for `sidecar.json` files:
336: 
337: ```
338: ~/.gemini/antigravity/sidecars/<name>/sidecar.json    ← Antigravity 2.0
339: ~/.gemini/jetski/sidecars/<name>/sidecar.json          ← Jetski / IDE
340: ```
341: 
342: > **These directories are inherently global.** There is no workspace-scoped sidecar discovery. This is the one place where the "nothing outside the plugin" rule can't fully apply — sidecars must be written to these runtime directories or Antigravity won't find them.
343: 
344: Each `<name>/` subdirectory represents one sidecar process. Antigravity reads the `sidecar.json` manifest and manages the process lifecycle.
345: 
346: ### Sidecar Manifest (`sidecar.json`)
347: 
348: A sidecar manifest defines what to run, how to schedule it, and what environment to provide:
349: 
350: ```json
351: {
352:   "builtin": "schedule",
353:   "args": ["*/10 * * * *", "/path/to/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py"],
354:   "restart_policy": "always",
355:   "display_name": "Bug Fixer Engineering (owner/repo)",
356:   "description": "Checks for eligible issues every 10 min.",
357:   "env": {
358:     "ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID": "project-uuid",
359:     "PATH": "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:...",
360:     "BUG_FIXER_CONFIG": "/path/to/workspace/config.json"
361:   }
362: }
363: ```
364: 
365: | Field | Type | Description |
366: |-------|------|-------------|
367: | `builtin` | string | The sidecar type. `"schedule"` runs on a cron schedule. |
368: | `args` | array | For `schedule`: `[cron_expression, script_path]`. The script is invoked by the scheduler on each cron tick. |
369: | `restart_policy` | string | `"always"` restarts the sidecar if it crashes. |
370: | `display_name` | string | Human-readable name shown in the Antigravity UI/dashboard. |
371: | `description` | string | Shown in sidecar listings. |
372: | `env` | object | Environment variables injected into the process. **Critical** — see below. |
373: 
374: ### Sidecar Execution Model
375: 
376: When a `schedule` sidecar fires:
377: 
378: 1. **Antigravity's scheduler** wakes up at the cron interval
379: 2. **Forks a subprocess** running the script specified in `args[1]`
380: 3. The script runs as a **plain Python process** — it is NOT an LLM conversation
381: 4. The script's `stdout`/`stderr` go to Antigravity's sidecar logs
382: 5. The script is expected to **exit quickly** (seconds, not minutes)
383: 6. If the script needs to do LLM work, it spawns a **new conversation** via `agentapi new-conversation`
384: 7. The `restart_policy: "always"` means the scheduler continues firing on the next cron tick even if the script exits with an error
385: 
386: ### The `env` Block is Critical
387: 
388: **Sidecars do NOT inherit the user's shell environment.** The sidecar process gets a minimal environment from Antigravity's runtime. Without an explicit `env` block:
389: 
390: - **`PATH` is minimal** — `agentapi`, `python3`, `gh`, and other CLI tools won't be found
391: - **`ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` is unset** — `agentapi new-conversation` fails because it doesn't know which project to spawn into
392: - **`BUG_FIXER_CONFIG` is unset** — scripts can't find the workspace config
393: 
394: This was the root cause of a production failure: the sidecar templates shipped without `env`, so the installed sidecars pointed to scripts that couldn't find `agentapi` on the `PATH`. All 9 sidecar configs (3 sidecars × 3 directories) were silently failing on every cron tick.
395: 
396: #### Required `env` Variables
397: 
398: | Variable | Purpose | How to resolve |
399: |----------|---------|---------------|
400: | `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` | Identifies the project for `agentapi` conversation spawning | Detected at install time from `~/.gemini/config/projects/*.json` or from the active Antigravity context |
401: | `PATH` | Full `PATH` including `~/.gemini/antigravity/bin/` (for `agentapi`) and `/usr/local/bin` (for `python3`, `gh`) | Snapshot of `$PATH` at install time |
402: | `BUG_FIXER_CONFIG` | Path to the workspace config file | Set to `<repo>/.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/config.json` |
403: 
404: #### Belt-and-Suspenders `PATH` Fix
405: 
406: Even with the `env` block, the dispatchers have a runtime fallback:
407: 
408: ```python
409: # Ensure agentapi is on PATH — sidecar scheduler may not inherit user's shell PATH
410: AGENTAPI_DIR = Path.home() / ".gemini" / "antigravity" / "bin"
411: if AGENTAPI_DIR.is_dir():
412:     os.environ["PATH"] = str(AGENTAPI_DIR) + os.pathsep + os.environ.get("PATH", "")
413: ```
414: 
415: This is defensive — the `env` block in the sidecar template is the proper solution, but keeping both provides resilience against `PATH` being partially set.
416: 
417: ### Sidecar Templates vs Installed Sidecars
418: 
419: The plugin repo contains **template** sidecar files with placeholders. The installer resolves them to absolute paths:
420: 
421: ```
422: plugin-repo/sidecars/bug-fixer-engineering-loop/sidecar.json           ← Template (placeholders)
423: ~/.gemini/antigravity/sidecars/bug-fixer-engineering-loop/sidecar.json  ← Installed (resolved)
424: ```
425: 
426: Placeholders resolved by `install.sh`:
427: 
428: | Placeholder | Resolved to | Example |
429: |-------------|-------------|---------|
430: | `<engineering_cron>` | Cron expression from config | `*/10 * * * *` |
431: | `<triage_cron>` | Cron expression from config | `0 * * * *` |
432: | `<architect_cron>` | Cron expression from config | `*/15 * * * *` |
433: | `<trajectory_review_cron>` | Cron expression from config | `0 18 * * *` |
434: | `<plugin_dir>` | Absolute path to the plugin directory | `/Users/me/project/.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-plugin` |
435: | `<owner/repo>` | GitHub `owner/repo` slug | `matthewmcneill/esp32-app-foundation` |
436: | `<project_id>` | `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` for conversation spawning | `a1b2c3d4-...` |
437: | `<path>` | Full `$PATH` snapshot from install time | `/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:...` |
438: | `<config_path>` | Absolute path to workspace `config.json` | `/Users/me/project/.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/config.json` |

440: ### Sidecar Lifecycle & Failure Modes
441: 
442: Understanding sidecar failure modes is essential for debugging:
443: 
444: | Failure Mode | Symptom | Root Cause | Fix |

465: ### Dispatcher Architecture (The Non-LLM Control Plane)
466: 
467: Dispatchers are the Python scripts invoked by sidecars. They are **pure control plane logic** — they never call the LLM themselves. Their sole job is to decide whether there's work to do and, if so, spawn an LLM conversation to handle it.
468: 
469: #### Why This Matters
470: 
471: Running an LLM conversation costs money and burns quota. If the sidecar directly launched an LLM conversation on every cron tick, you'd spend tokens even when there's nothing to do. The dispatcher pattern keeps costs at zero when idle:
472: 
473: ```
474: Cron fires → Dispatcher runs  → No eligible issues → Exit immediately (cost: $0)
475: Cron fires → Dispatcher runs  → 2 eligible issues  → Spawn 2 conversations (cost: ~$0.50)
476: ```
477: 
478: #### Dispatcher Flow (Engineering — the most complex)
479: 
480: ```
481: 1.  Load config from workspace (WORKSPACE_CONFIG only — no plugin root fallback)
482: 2.  Derive REPO_DIR, STATE_DIR, PLUGIN_DIR from config file location
483: 3.  Check circuit breaker — if cooldown.json exists and not expired, exit immediately
484: 4.  Recover stale claims (3-layer detection):
485:     a. Claim file exists but has no conversation_id (spawn failed mid-write)
486:     b. Claim file older than TTL (conversation ran too long or was killed)
487:     c. Conversation exists but is in terminal state (idle/errored/cancelled)
488: 5.  Count active bug-fixer PRs via safe_ingest.py — if >= max_concurrent, exit
489: 6.  Query GitHub for eligible issues (via safe_ingest.py):
490:     - Has "auto-fixable" label
491:     - Not in exclusion_labels (e.g., "human-required", "P1-blocker", "hardware-required")
492:     - Not already claimed (no active claim file)
493:     - Sorted by priority (milestone boost, label priority ranking)
494: 7.  For each eligible issue (up to max_concurrent - active_prs):
495:     a. Write claim file to STATE_DIR/claims/<issue_number>.json (atomic lock)
496:     b. Add "status:in-progress" label to the GitHub issue
497:     c. Build the skill prompt (read SKILL.md, inject config values)
498:     d. Spawn LLM conversation via: agentapi new-conversation --system-prompt <skill> --user-prompt <issue>
499:     e. Capture conversation_id from agentapi stdout
500:     f. Update claim file with conversation_id
501:     g. If spawn fails: remove claim file, remove label, log error
502: 8.  Track spawn success/failure for circuit breaker
503: 9.  Log summary and exit
504: ```
505: 
506: #### Spawning Conversations via `agentapi`
507: 
508: The dispatchers use `agentapi new-conversation` to launch LLM sessions:
509: 
510: ```python
511: cmd = [
512:     "agentapi", "new-conversation",
513:     "--system-prompt", skill_text,
514:     "--user-prompt", prompt_text,
515: ]
516: r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
517: ```
518: 
519: The `agentapi` tool is Antigravity's CLI for programmatic conversation management. It:
520: - Creates a new conversation in the Antigravity runtime
521: - Injects the skill as the system prompt
522: - Injects the issue details as the user prompt
523: - Returns a JSON object with `conversationId` that can be used to monitor progress
524: - Requires `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID` to know which project context to use
525: 
526: A successful spawn returns:
527: ```json
528: {"conversationId": "ec33ebf9-0cba-4100-8142-c61503f6c587"}
529: ```
530: 
531: A failed spawn (quota exhausted, missing env vars, etc.) returns a non-zero exit code and error text on stderr.

533: #### Stale Claim Recovery
534: 
535: The engineering dispatcher implements 3-layer stale claim detection to handle conversations that crash, timeout, or are killed:
536: 
537: ```python
538: # Layer 1: Claim file has no conversation ID (spawn failed mid-write)
539: if not claim_data.get("conversation_id"):
540:     recover(claim)
541: 
542: # Layer 2: Claim file older than TTL (conversation ran too long)
543: if claim_age > CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS:
544:     recover(claim)
545: 
546: # Layer 3: Conversation exists but is in terminal state
547: status = get_conversation_status(conversation_id)
548: if status in ("idle", "errored", "cancelled"):
549:     recover(claim)
550: ```
551: 
552: Recovery means:
553: 1. Remove the claim file from `STATE_DIR/claims/`
554: 2. Remove the `status:in-progress` label from the GitHub issue
555: 3. The issue becomes eligible for the next engineering cycle

570: ## Circuit Breakers
571: 
572: When the LLM quota runs out, dispatchers can enter a catastrophic failure loop:
573: 
574: 1. **Engineering loop fires** (every 10 minutes)
575: 2. **Finds eligible issues**, writes claim files, adds `status:in-progress` labels
576: 3. **Spawns `agentapi new-conversation`** — all calls fail (quota exhausted)
577: 4. **Removes claim files**, removes labels (cleanup on failure)
578: 5. **Next cycle fires** — same issues are eligible again
579: 6. **Labels churn** on GitHub (added/removed every 10 minutes), user is spammed with dozens of failing conversation notifications
580: 7. **Repeat indefinitely** until quota is restored or the sidecar is manually stopped
581: 
582: ### Implementation
583: 
584: Each dispatcher tracks consecutive spawn failures using two files in the workspace state directory:
585: 
586: | File | Purpose | Format |
587: |------|---------|--------|
588: | `failure_count` | Number of consecutive cycles where all spawns failed | Plain text integer |
589: | `cooldown.json` | Present only when cooling down | JSON with `reason`, `entered_at`, `expires_at`, `expires_at_iso` |
590: 
591: #### Startup Check
592: 
593: ```python
594: COOLDOWN_FILE = STATE_DIR / "cooldown.json"
595: FAILURE_COUNT_FILE = STATE_DIR / "failure_count"
596: MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 3
597: COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 3600  # 1 hour
598: 
599: # Circuit breaker: check cooldown before doing any work
600: if COOLDOWN_FILE.exists():
601:     try:
602:         cooldown = json.loads(COOLDOWN_FILE.read_text())
603:         if time.time() < cooldown.get("expires_at", 0):
604:             log(f"ENGINEERING_EXIT: Cooling down until {cooldown['expires_at_iso']} — "
605:                 f"reason: {cooldown['reason']}")
606:             sys.exit(0)
607:         # Cooldown expired, clean up and resume normal operation
608:         COOLDOWN_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
609:         FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
610:     except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
611:         COOLDOWN_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
612: ```
613: 
614: #### Post-Spawn Tracking
615: 
616: ```python
617: # After the spawn loop completes:
618: if spawned == 0 and len(eligible) > 0:
619:     # Had work to do but couldn't spawn anything — this is a failure
620:     try:
621:         count = int(FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.read_text().strip()) + 1 \
622:             if FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.exists() else 1
623:     except (ValueError, OSError):
624:         count = 1
625:     STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
626:     FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.write_text(str(count))
627:     if count >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES:
628:         expires = time.time() + COOLDOWN_SECONDS
629:         COOLDOWN_FILE.write_text(json.dumps({
630:             "reason": f"{count} consecutive spawn failures",
631:             "entered_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
632:             "expires_at": expires,
633:             "expires_at_iso": datetime.fromtimestamp(expires, timezone.utc).isoformat(),
634:         }))
635:         log(f"Circuit breaker tripped after {count} consecutive failures. "
636:             f"Cooling down for {COOLDOWN_SECONDS}s.")
637: else:
638:     # At least one spawn succeeded, or no eligible work — reset counter
639:     FAILURE_COUNT_FILE.unlink(missing_ok=True)
640: ```
641: 
642: #### Cooldown File Format
643: 
644: ```json
645: {
646:   "reason": "3 consecutive spawn failures",
647:   "entered_at": "2026-09-27T14:30:00+00:00",
648:   "expires_at": 1727447400.0,
649:   "expires_at_iso": "2026-09-27T15:30:00+00:00"
650: }
651: ```

653: #### Behaviour Summary
654: 
655: | Cycle # | Eligible Issues | Spawned | Failure Count | Action |
656: |:------:|:--------------:|:-------:|:-------------:|--------|
657: | 1 | 3 | 0 (quota fail) | 1 | Continue |
658: | 2 | 3 | 0 (quota fail) | 2 | Continue |
659: | 3 | 3 | 0 (quota fail) | 3 | **Trip breaker** — write `cooldown.json`, stop for 1 hour |
660: | 4–9 | — | — | — | Exit immediately (cooldown active) |
661: | 10 | 3 | 2 (quota restored) | 0 | Reset counter, normal operation resumes |
662: | 11 | 0 | 0 (no work) | 0 | No increment — counter only tracks "had work but couldn't do it" |

690: ## Anti-Patterns (Learned the Hard Way)
691: 
692: ### 1. Writing to Global Config
693: 
694: **Problem:** `install.sh` wrote hooks, rules, scripts, and skills to `~/.gemini/config/`. A broken global hook bricked every project on the machine. When an agent ran `git clean` and deleted the plugin directory, the global hook pointed to a missing script, blocking all tool execution across the entire installation.
695: 
696: **Fix:** Only write workspace-scoped artefacts. Scripts and skills are used in-place.
697: 
698: ### 2. Absolute Paths in Config
699: 
700: **Problem:** `config.json` contained `/Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/...` — completely non-portable. Can't be committed, can't be shared.
701: 
702: **Fix:** Derive paths from the config file's own location. The standardised directory layout makes every path computable at runtime.
703: 
704: ### 3. Instance Values in Plugin Root
705: 
706: **Problem:** `config.json` with `target_repo`, `repo_dir`, and `maintainer` lived in the plugin root. This meant:
707: - Dirty submodule after configuration
708: - Instance values committed to the plugin repo
709: - Only one project could use the plugin at a time
710: 
711: **Fix:** Config lives in the workspace directory (sibling of the plugin submodule). Plugin root contains no instance-specific files.
712: 
713: ### 4. No Circuit Breaker
714: 
715: **Problem:** When LLM quota ran out, the engineering dispatcher fired every 10 minutes, spawned conversations that all failed, churned issue labels on GitHub, and spammed the user with failing conversations.
716: 
717: **Fix:** Track consecutive spawn failures. After 3 failures, write a cooldown file and stop dispatching for 1 hour.
718: 
719: ### 5. Project-Specific Rules in Generic Plugin
720: 
721: **Problem:** Rule 16 ("PlatformIO MCP Lock Discipline") was in the plugin's `rules/AGENTS.md`. Every consumer — including Node.js, Rails, or plain Python projects — inherited a PlatformIO-specific rule.
722: 
723: **Fix:** Replace with a generic "Respect Project Testing Rules" rule. PlatformIO specifics go in the consumer's `.agents/rules/`.
724: 
725: ### 6. Copying Files Instead of Using In-Place
726: 
727: **Problem:** `install.sh` copied skills to `~/.gemini/config/skills/` AND `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/`, with `sed` templating to bake in absolute paths. This created 12+ duplicate skill directories that drifted out of sync with the source.
728: 
729: **Fix:** Skills are used directly from the plugin directory. Antigravity discovers them via the plugin's `plugin.json` manifest.
730: 
731: ### 7. Missing Sidecar `env` Block
732: 
733: **Problem:** Sidecar templates had no `env` field. The sidecar scheduler doesn't inherit the user's shell `PATH`, so `agentapi` couldn't be found.
734: 
735: **Fix:** Add explicit `env` block with `ANTIGRAVITY_PROJECT_ID`, `PATH`, and `BUG_FIXER_CONFIG`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# migrate_labels.sh — Rename bug-fixer labels on a target repo
# Usage: ./scripts/migrate_labels.sh <owner/repo> [--dry-run]
#
# This script renames old-style bug-fixer labels to the new
# bug-fixer:<actor>:<name> routed-segment namespace.
# Uses `gh label create --force` which renames in-place.

TARGET_REPO="${1:-}"
if [[ -z "$TARGET_REPO" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: migrate_labels.sh <owner/repo> [--dry-run]"
  exit 1
fi

DRY_RUN=false
if [[ "${2:-}" == "--dry-run" ]]; then
  DRY_RUN=true
fi

declare -A RENAME_MAP=(
  ["auto-fixable"]="bug-fixer:engineer:needs-fix"
  ["human-required"]="bug-fixer:human:required"
  ["needs-approach-review"]="bug-fixer:human:needs-approach-review"
  ["project-candidate"]="bug-fixer:human:project-candidate"
  ["input-needed"]="bug-fixer:human:input-needed"
  ["status:in-progress"]="bug-fixer:engineer:in-progress"
  ["status:awaiting-review"]="bug-fixer:architect:awaiting-review"
  ["bug-fixer"]="bug-fixer:engineer:pr"
  ["bug-fixer-health"]="bug-fixer:system:health"
  ["spec-change-request"]="bug-fixer:human:spec-change-request"
  ["needs-iteration"]="bug-fixer:engineer:needs-iteration"
  ["architect-approved"]="bug-fixer:architect:approved"
  ["needs-human-intervention"]="bug-fixer:human:needs-intervention"
  ["discovered-in-review"]="bug-fixer:triage:discovered-in-review"
  ["complexity:mechanical"]="bug-fixer:complexity:mechanical"
  ["complexity:standard"]="bug-fixer:complexity:standard"
  ["complexity:architect"]="bug-fixer:complexity:architect"
)

declare -A LABELS_META=(
  ["bug-fixer:engineer:needs-fix"]="0E8A16:Issues eligible for autonomous fixing"
  ["bug-fixer:human:required"]="D93F0B:Issues requiring human intervention or architectural review"
  ["bug-fixer:human:needs-approach-review"]="FBCA04:Fix approach requires human maintainer sign-off"
  ["bug-fixer:human:project-candidate"]="5319E7:Large multi-step initiative candidate"
  ["bug-fixer:human:input-needed"]="D4C5F9:Waiting for human input or clarification"
  ["bug-fixer:engineer:in-progress"]="1D76DB:Currently being worked on by an agent or human"
  ["bug-fixer:engineer:pr"]="0075CA:Managed by autonomous bug-fixer loop"
  ["bug-fixer:system:health"]="C5DEF5:Bug fixer health, metrics, or diagnostic report"
  ["bug-fixer:human:spec-change-request"]="F9D0C4:Proposed modification to design specification"
  ["bug-fixer:engineer:needs-iteration"]="E4E669:PR needs engineering rework after architect review"
  ["bug-fixer:architect:approved"]="0E8A16:Architect approved the PR for merge"
  ["bug-fixer:architect:awaiting-review"]="BFD4F2:PR ready for architect review"
  ["bug-fixer:human:needs-intervention"]="D93F0B:Architect escalated — needs human resolution"
  ["bug-fixer:triage:discovered-in-review"]="d4c5f9:Auto-filed during PR review, requires human approval before auto-fix"
  ["bug-fixer:complexity:mechanical"]="ffffff:Model tier: rote/deterministic work"
  ["bug-fixer:complexity:standard"]="ffffff:Model tier: standard engineering work"
  ["bug-fixer:complexity:architect"]="ffffff:Model tier: needs architect-grade reasoning"
)

for old_label in "${!RENAME_MAP[@]}"; do
  new_label="${RENAME_MAP[$old_label]}"
  meta="${LABELS_META[$new_label]:-ededed:Managed by bug-fixer-loop}"
  color="${meta%%:*}"
  description="${meta#*:}"

  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "[DRY RUN] Would rename: '${old_label}' → '${new_label}' (${color})"
  else
    echo "Renaming: '${old_label}' → '${new_label}'"
    # Create new label (in-place if same name, or creates new one)
    gh label create "${new_label}" --repo "${TARGET_REPO}" --force \
      --color "${color}" --description "${description}" 2>/dev/null || true
    
    # Delete the old label if it differs from the new one (case-insensitive check)
    if [[ "${old_label,,}" != "${new_label,,}" ]]; then
      gh label delete "${old_label}" --repo "${TARGET_REPO}" --yes 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  fi
done

echo ""
echo "Migration complete. Verify at: https://github.com/${TARGET_REPO}/labels"
